Hi Emma / Rajiv — great to meet you both. Short recap + what we are attaching: 

Recap from call:
- Scope: 6-week pilot to validate EHR summarization and triage prompts.
- SLO target: p95 end-to-end latency < 1.2s for a 256-token prompt + 128-token response.
- Quality guardrail: target intent accuracy > 92% and hallucination rate < 2% on the seed prompt set.

What’s attached (and links below):
- Redwood-verified perf profiles (PDF): consolidated p50/p95 + reqs/sec for the recommended models at seq lengths 128/256/512. Profiles include test hardware (A100 v4 80GB) and trace artifacts.
- Prompt pack (zip): 15 seed prompts we use for initial regression checks and quality baselines.
- Bench traces (json): raw traces you can feed into your sizing tool.

Quick model recs for pilot (shortlist):
1) Redwood-R2-7B-q4 (recommended default) — best cost-to-quality tradeoff for triage + summarization. Verified at seq256 (prompt+gen) in our hosted run: ~42 reqs/sec, p50 210ms, p95 540ms. Quality: extractive F1 ~0.89 on our clinical summarization set, hallucination ~1.4%.
2) Redwood-R2-13B-int8 (higher fidelity) — for cases where punch-through accuracy matters: ~18 reqs/sec, p50 420ms, p95 980ms. Quality: F1 ~0.92, hallucination ~0.9%.
3) Redwood-R2-7B-clip (fast variant) — low-latency fallback for burst traffic: ~78 reqs/sec, p50 120ms, p95 320ms; expect minor drop in abstractive fluency.

Regression guardrails we recommend (quick list):
- Daily micro-evals (15 prompts) with alerts if avg hallucination delta > 0.8 percentage points or intent accuracy drops > 2 points.
- Canary rollout: 5% traffic for 24 hrs, compare QA metrics -> auto-rollback trigger on regressions.
- Prefix caching for frequent templates (saves ~25–40% token cost without affecting latency SLOs).

Links: https://app.redwood.ai/perf-profiles/VDH-demo-20280418 (profiles + low-level traces)
Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c_benchpack (prompt pack + bench traces)
HubSpot: https://hubspot.example/s/VDH-12345

Next steps I suggest:
- Ben will drop the full bench traces + a condensed readiness checklist.
- If the numbers look good to your infra team, we’ll schedule a sizing call with engineering (30m) — propose Wed 04/20 at 11:00 PT.

I’ll attach the PDFs & traces to this thread. Ping if you want a one-pager slide for your procurement team.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Demo follow-up + ask on perf/quality guardrails

Emma / team — adding the bench artifacts and a short ops checklist. A few operational notes you’ll find in the traces: 

Perf highlights (hosted baseline, seq256 prompt + 128 gen) — these are Redwood-verified under controlled load: 
- Redwood-R2-7B-q4: 42 reqs/sec (avg), p50 210ms, p95 540ms, 128-token generation throughput ~370 tokens/sec per GPU.
- Redwood-R2-13B-int8: 18 reqs/sec (avg), p50 420ms, p95 980ms, 128-token gen throughput ~210 tokens/sec per GPU.
- R2-7B-clip (fast): 78 reqs/sec (avg), p50 120ms, p95 320ms — intended as graceful degradation option.

Sizing quick guide (for pilot 100 rps peak with 20% burst tolerance): 
- If you need 100 concurrent requests of workload above, recommended starting point: 4 x A100 v4 (shared via Redwood Dedicated) + autoscaler config (scale buffer 30%). Exact needs vary by average sequence length; we included a sizing calc in the bench traces file.

Quality/regression setup (what we included):
- Prompt pack: 15 prompts, each labeled with expected intent and golden outputs where applicable.
- Micro-eval harness: small script + aggregated metrics (intent accuracy, extractive F1, hallucination rate, ROUGE-L).
- Alert thresholds: default suggested thresholds in the PDF (we can tune these with you).

Attachments: bench_traces_seq256_to_512.json (contains request traces, kernel profiles, and sample outputs), veridian_prompt_pack_v1.zip

If it helps, I can import the prompt pack into a shared notebook and run an initial baseline against your sample subset — needs a 1-hour pairing call.

Thanks,
Ben Carter

- Bench environment: traces were run in our standard hosted testbed (network egress constrained to 250Mbps per-node to approximate VPC-limited setups). We annotated network usage in bench_traces_seq256_to_512.json. Expect ~40–60MB/min throughput under sustained 128-token generations per second.
- Alerts: yes — the micro-eval harness supports webhooks. We can push alerts to PagerDuty and a Slack channel (we’ll include a sample PagerDuty integration playbook).
